plan: NO POSITION. Not an entry candidate under the quality-at-own-history-discount frame: at a 13-week high, +34% 1y, 12% off the 52w high, 52w low is 329 days old, and FY26 earnings are at a 5-year peak. Separately the cheapness is a consolidation artifact - shareholder multiple is ~31x earnings, not 10.6x EV/EBIT. Entry friction ~200bp all-in (0% AIM stamp + half of a 400bp touch), $20,759/day max order vs $24,750 for a 0.75% position, and a >10% holder (Soros, ~88 median days of volume) actively reducing. Revisit only if the price re-rates back toward the 73-80p area WITH China stabilised and one pipeline product commercialised.

edge_explainer: The screen ranked EAH 16th on 10.6x EV/EBIT, 5.8% FCF yield, 0.79x book and +20% net cash. Every one of those is arithmetically defensible and economically misleading. (1) About half of group EBITDA comes from ECO Biok, a 51%-owned Chinese subsidiary - the company's own FY25 disaggregation shows Biok adjusted EBITDA GBP 3.7m of a group GBP 7.3m - and 36% of FY25 group profit went to the 49% minority (GBP 948k of GBP 2,634k). The screen does add minority interest to EV at book (66.715 + 5.062 - 18.635 + 7.633 = 60.775, verified), but adding GBP 7.6m of book MI does not neutralise consolidating 100% of that subsidiary's EBIT. (2) The effective tax rate is 34% (China dividend withholding plus unrelieved parent losses), so EBIT converts to attributable earnings at roughly 38%. Result: FY26 attributable earnings of about GBP 2.21m (basic EPS 3.26p x 67.71m weighted shares) against a GBP 67.8m market cap = a statutory P/E near 31x, versus 12.4x on attributable EBIT and 9.7x on the fully consolidated figure. (3) Net cash is real (GBP 25.4m against GBP 5.0m of lease liabilities and no drawn borrowings) but GBP 11.4m of it sits inside ECO Biok, which the Board itself describes as 'unavailable to the Group outside of China' and which is subject to Chinese exchange control; usable cash outside China is GBP 14.0m and was GBP 14.0m a year earlier too, because the core business exactly funds the R&D programme. On top of that, the frame simply does not apply: the stock is at a three-month high after a 34% year, the 52-week low is 329 days old, and FY26 revenue (+10%), gross margin (48.6%, a third straight year of expansion) and EPS (+31%) are all improving. This is not a de-rate and not a derailment - it is a decent small pharma that is fairly to fully priced, in a name with a 400bp touch, a $20.8k daily order cap and an active >10% seller. Two genuine long-run risks were confirmed rather than resolved: Aivlosin is 91.6% of revenue with no composition-of-matter protection and the company's own risk register rates the generic threat HIGH likelihood / HIGH impact; and China, which drove four consecutive years of revenue decline before stabilising in FY26, was singled out in the 15-Jul-2026 outlook as the one place trading is not in line.
